# Fixtures for the importers and adapters

These files are data, never code. Tests read them and never execute them.

- `promptfoo/sample-export.json`: verbatim from promptfoo, `test/__fixtures__/sample-export.json` (MIT licence). Two providers, two tests, every result a failure.
- `promptfoo/synthetic-redteam-repeat.json`: synthetic (10.5 KB), written to the field names in promptfoo 0.125.1 `src/evaluator.ts:1403-1409,3166-3168` (`result.metadata`, `repeatGroupId`, `repeatIndex`) and `src/redteam/index.ts:549,556,736-743` (`pluginId`, `severity`, `strategyId`); no real export with a repeat or a red-team row exists upstream. One provider and three tests: a harmful-plugin test with three repeats written in completion order (`repeatIndex` 2, 0, 1; passes at 0 and 2, fails at 1) carrying `pluginId`, `strategyId`, `severity` and `harmCategory` in both the row's `metadata` and `testCase.metadata`; a PII test with `pluginId` only on the test case and `severity` only on the row; and an ordinary test whose only metadata is a `harmCategory`.
- `inspect/log_formats.json`: verbatim from Inspect AI, `tests/log/test_eval_log/log_formats.json` (MIT licence). One model, one sample. The `.eval` zip form is built from it inside the tests.
- `inspect/log_message_deduplication.eval`: verbatim from Inspect AI, `tests/log/test_eval_log/log_message_deduplication.eval` at tag 0.3.289 (https://raw.githubusercontent.com/UKGovernmentBEIS/inspect_ai/0.3.289/tests/log/test_eval_log/log_message_deduplication.eval, MIT licence); 8.1 KB, written by inspect_ai 0.3.135.dev2. One sample, 42 events, five `ToolEvent`s (`bash`, `{"cmd": "ls"}`, id `hardcoded_0`), no tool errors and no `attachment://` references; it is the real file the trace tests read. Attachment, error and condensed-log paths are tested with events written in the test, to the field names in `event/_tool.py` and `log/_condense.py`.
- `garak/quack.report.jsonl`: verbatim from garak, `tests/_assets/analyze/quack.report.jsonl` at tag v0.17.1 (https://raw.githubusercontent.com/NVIDIA/garak/v0.17.1/tests/_assets/analyze/quack.report.jsonl, Apache-2.0 licence); 10.4 KB, written by garak 0.14.0.pre1 with the `test` generator. One probe, one prompt, one generation, one detector (`lmrc.QuackMedicine`, score 0.0); the attempt is written at status 1 and status 2; the file has no hit, no `run.eval_threshold` and no target name.
- `garak/synthetic-0.17.report.jsonl`: synthetic, written to the field names in garak v0.17.1 `attempt.py:268-301` and `evaluators/base.py:213-245` (no real post-0.13 report with a hit or more than one generation exists). Three generations per attempt, a `run.eval_threshold` of 0.6, a score of 0.55 that passes at 0.6 and is a hit at 0.5, a `null` output, a multi-turn prompt, a repeated prompt, one attempt with no status-2 row, and `eval` rows counted from its own scores.
- `garak/synthetic-legacy-0.9.report.jsonl`: synthetic, in the 0.9.0.6 shape (a `config` row, string `prompt` and `outputs`, integer scores, `eval` rows with `total`), modelled on the real 0.9.0.6 report linked from garak's `docs/source/report.rst`, which is 18.9 MB and so is not copied here.
- `adk/synthetic.evalset_result.json`: synthetic (20 KB), written to the field names in google-adk v2.14.1 `src/google/adk/evaluation/eval_result.py:31-96`, `eval_metrics.py:47-55,518-555` and `eval_case.py:33-154`, in the snake_case, int-enum, `model_dump_json(indent=2)` form `local_eval_set_results_manager.py:68-69` writes. No real `*.evalset_result.json` exists in the ADK repository, tests or docs (only the first 200 characters of one in https://github.com/google/adk-python/issues/3869), so this one is invented: values are made up and the key set is the model's, not a captured file's. Two eval cases of two runs each, listed in completion order (`repetition_index` 1 before 0 for the first case); one run has `session_details.events`, the others do not; `invocation_events` and `tool_uses` / `tool_responses` forms; one tool response with an `error`; statuses 1, 2, 3 and 4 and a 1-5 metric.
- `adk/synthetic-legacy-double-encoded.evalset_result.json`: synthetic (11 KB), the same result as `adk/synthetic.evalset_result.json` written the way ADK did before v1.22.0 (fix `fc4e3d6f60`, https://github.com/google/adk-python/commit/fc4e3d6f60): `json.dumps(model_dump_json())`, a JSON string holding the object's compact JSON text (the shape of the issue #3869 excerpt). The tests check it imports as the same run as the plain file.
- `adk/basic_criteria.home_automation.evalset.json`: verbatim from google/adk-python, `contributing/samples/evaluation/basic_criteria/home_automation.evalset.json` at tag v2.14.1 (https://raw.githubusercontent.com/google/adk-python/v2.14.1/contributing/samples/evaluation/basic_criteria/home_automation.evalset.json, Apache-2.0 licence); 1.7 KB, an `EvalSet` (a dataset, not a result), two single-turn cases. The result importer is tested to refuse it, and `import-dataset adk` reads it.
- `adk/rubric_criteria.home_automation.evalset.json`: verbatim from google/adk-python, `contributing/samples/evaluation/rubric_criteria/home_automation.evalset.json` at tag v2.14.1 (https://raw.githubusercontent.com/google/adk-python/v2.14.1/contributing/samples/evaluation/rubric_criteria/home_automation.evalset.json, Apache-2.0 licence); 937 bytes, an `EvalSet` with one single-turn case (`list_bedroom_devices`). Despite the directory name its cases carry no `rubrics`: the rubrics of that sample are in its `eval_config.json`, which `import-dataset` does not read.
- `adk/test_file_vs_evalset.multi_session.evalset.json`: verbatim from google/adk-python, `contributing/samples/evaluation/test_file_vs_evalset/multi_session.evalset.json` at tag v2.14.1 (https://raw.githubusercontent.com/google/adk-python/v2.14.1/contributing/samples/evaluation/test_file_vs_evalset/multi_session.evalset.json, Apache-2.0 licence); 2.3 KB, an `EvalSet` with a two-invocation case (`list_then_turn_off`, a tool call in each invocation) and a single-turn one (`set_bedroom_temperature`).
- `adk/test_file_vs_evalset.single_turn.test.json`: verbatim from google/adk-python, `contributing/samples/evaluation/test_file_vs_evalset/single_turn.test.json` at tag v2.14.1 (https://raw.githubusercontent.com/google/adk-python/v2.14.1/contributing/samples/evaluation/test_file_vs_evalset/single_turn.test.json, Apache-2.0 licence); 947 bytes. Named like the legacy `*.test.json` files but it holds an `EvalSet` (one case, `kitchen_temperature`), not the flat list.
- `adk/home_automation_agent.simple_test2.test.json`: verbatim from google/adk-python, `tests/integration/fixture/home_automation_agent/simple_test2.test.json` at tag v2.14.1 (https://raw.githubusercontent.com/google/adk-python/v2.14.1/tests/integration/fixture/home_automation_agent/simple_test2.test.json, Apache-2.0 licence); 250 bytes, the flat legacy list (`query`, `expected_tool_use`, `reference`) with one item. The upstream directory name is a prefix of the local name so that it does not clash with the other files; it is the only real file of the legacy list shape found.
- `adk/user_simulation.home_automation.evalset.json`: verbatim from google/adk-python, `contributing/samples/evaluation/user_simulation/home_automation.evalset.json` at tag v2.14.1 (https://raw.githubusercontent.com/google/adk-python/v2.14.1/contributing/samples/evaluation/user_simulation/home_automation.evalset.json, Apache-2.0 licence); 1.2 KB, an `EvalSet` of two `conversation_scenario` cases and no `conversation`. `import-dataset adk` skips both and then refuses the file.
- `adk/synthetic-mixed.evalset.json`: synthetic (3.7 KB), written to the field names in google-adk v2.14.1 `eval_set.py:24-41`, `eval_case.py:97-154,190-236` and `eval_metrics.py` (`Rubric`, `RubricContent`); every value is invented. It exists for what the real files leave out: three eval cases, the first with two invocations, `session_input.state`, case-level and invocation-level `rubrics` (one with a `type`, two without), the second written in camelCase with the `invocation_events` form of a call, and the third a `conversation_scenario` case, so that the skip warning is tested on a file that also has cases to import.
- `claude-plugin-eval/aggregate-result.json`: synthetic (13.4 KB), written to the field names of the `aggregate-result.json` writer schema in Claude Code 2.1.322 (`schemaVersion` 1; introduced in 2.1.269) and the descriptions in https://code.claude.com/docs/en/plugin-evals ("Read the results", "JSON result"). The docs show no sample file, so every value is invented. Three cases: `commit-message` (two runs per arm, from the evidence's constructed example: an `llm` grader and a `withOnly` `tool_used` Skill grader that has `scored: false`), `rename-symbol` (a with-arm run with `error: "timed out after 300s"` that was still graded, and a without-arm run with an `aborted` mock and no graders) and `explain-stack-trace` (two runs of a `with` arm only, with no `arms.without` key, to exercise a case that has no runs in the baseline arm). `costUsd` includes `judgeCostUsd` as the docs say; some runs carry no `durationSeconds`; `partial` is false.
- `deepeval/test_run.json`: synthetic, written to the schema in DeepEval's `test_run/test_run.py` and `api.py`; it has a metric error, a positional `test_case_N` name and a conversational case.
- `lm-eval/<model>/samples_<task>_<time>.jsonl`: synthetic, written to the record shape built in lm-evaluation-harness `evaluator.py` and `loggers/evaluation_tracker.py`; `gpt2` has one filter, `llama3` has two.
- `table/long.csv`, `table/long.jsonl`, `table/wide.csv`: synthetic, for the generic importers (two systems, an error row, an undecided cell).
- `otel/trace.json`: verbatim from open-telemetry/opentelemetry-proto, `examples/trace.json` at commit `94f2f2d5f39c5139141dc7e564daa84aa2826531` (Apache-2.0 licence). One OTLP/JSON span; it shows the encoding (upper-case hex ids, string nanosecond times, kind and status as integers) and carries no agent attributes.
- `otel/genai-content-on.json`, `otel/genai-content-off.json`: synthetic, built from the GenAI semantic conventions (semantic-conventions-genai `docs/gen-ai/execute-tool.md` and `client-inference.md`), as OTLP/JSON. The first has arguments, results and `gen_ai.output.messages`, with its spans in reverse order; the second has none of them, as with `OTEL_INSTRUMENTATION_GENAI_CAPTURE_MESSAGE_CONTENT=NO_CONTENT`.
- `otel/openinference.json`: synthetic, built from the OpenInference semantic conventions 0.1.45 (`spec/semantic_conventions.md`, flattened `llm.output_messages.N.message.content`). Whether a real `TOOL` span sets `input.value` and `output.value` is not verified.
- `otel/adk-schema-1.json`: synthetic, built from Google ADK 2.14.1 `telemetry/tracing.py` (`call_llm`, `gcp.vertex.agent.tool_call_args`, `gcp.vertex.agent.tool_response`). The attributes of the `call_llm` span itself are not verified, so it carries only `gcp.vertex.agent.event_id`.
- `otel/vercel-legacy.json`: synthetic, built from the Vercel AI SDK 7 `LegacyOpenTelemetry` documentation (`ai.toolCall.*`, `ai.usage.promptTokens`, `ai.response.text`).
- `otel/collector.jsonl`: synthetic, the same trace as `genai-content-on.json` in two batches, one OTLP/JSON object per line, as the collector's `file` exporter writes with `format: json`.
- `otel/sdk-console-concatenated.json`: synthetic, the same trace as five pretty-printed objects in a row, in the Python SDK's `span.to_json()` form (`0x` ids, ISO times, flat attributes), as `ConsoleSpanExporter` prints them.
- `otel/two-traces.json`: synthetic, the GenAI trace and a second three-span trace (two traceIds) in one OTLP/JSON object.
- `datasets/<format>/*`: synthetic, for `import-dataset`. Each is written by hand to the fields the tool documents for its test cases (promptfoo's `promptfooconfig.yaml`, `tests:` files and `__expected` CSV columns; DeepEval goldens; Ragas v2 and v1 samples; LangSmith examples; OpenAI Evals `samples.jsonl` and platform `item` lines; Inspect samples with `choices` and list targets; Braintrust records; Langfuse items; Phoenix examples), plus `jsonl/qa.jsonl` and `csv/qa.csv` for the generic readers. No real exported file was available for any of them, so every value is invented and the shapes are as documented, not verified against a file the tool wrote.
